159	### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty
160	
161	```gdscript
162	class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
163	enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
164	var phase: Phase
165	var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
166	func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
167	func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key layout: ADR-0004 § 3
168	func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void   # P5 event record; ADR-0004 § 5
169	func has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool           # true from the first granted open_for of that block until the scope is re-armed (ADR-0005 § 5.3)
170	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
171	```
172	
173	The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.
174	
175	| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
176	|---|---|---|
177	| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
178	| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
179	| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
180	| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
181	| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
182	| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |
183	
184	`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.
185	
186	`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. The debug-build check that catches a missed mark is ADR-0004 § 7 (it compares a block's hash with the kernel's `touch_serial` and with whether any key was marked, for blocks that do not declare `quiet_writes_allowed`); this ADR no longer states the rule. `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty`: it needs an open block and its records are discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE` and `CLOSED` (ADR-0004 § 5). `has_opened` is a pure read used by the kernel's hash path (ADR-0005 § 5.3): it never opens anything and never counts a violation. `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.
187	
188	### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback
189	
190	**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).
191	
192	- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
193	- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.
194	
195	**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.
196	
197	**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.
198	
199	**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.
200	
201	### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants
202	
203	A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.

245	
246	### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet
247	
248	The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).
249	
250	`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get_view(block_id: StringName) -> Object` (never `get`: a method named `get` overrides the native `Object.get()`, which is a load-time parse error on 4.7.2, probed, and ADR-0010's `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE` rule), returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get_view` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get_view(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.
251	
252	A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.
253	
254	### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule
255	
256	At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:
257	
258	1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
259	2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
260	3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
261	4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.
262	
263	**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.
264	
265	### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table
266	
267	States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).
268	
269	- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
270	- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
271	- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
272	- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
273	- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.
274	
275	The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.
276	
277	### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)
278	
279	Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).
280	
281	*(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07.)* The H1 **registries** group also holds, by name: `touch_serial` (a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`, written by every granted `open_for`; ADR-0004 § 7), the **hash-cache arrays** (`{hash, enc_len, serial}` as three parallel `PackedInt64Array`s sized once at the freeze; ADR-0005 §§ 5.1, 5.2), the per-block key-space table (ADR-0004 § 3) and the subscription tables (ADR-0004 § 2). **kernel_state** also holds the kernel-internal hash `SnapshotContext` of § 3 and the `kernel.clock` below. The H1 lint's fixed list is extended by exactly these names.
282	
283	**The `kernel.clock` view.** `kernel.clock` is an H1 member owned by this ADR. It carries `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` and is exposed to modules and the composition root only as a read-only view (getters `tick()`, `world_seed()`, `restore_epoch()`; no setters). `T` advances only in the tick driver's boundary. **`world_seed`** is set before `INIT` (by `request_new_game`, or from the payload by `request_restore`) and does not change until the next new game or restore. **`restore_epoch`** is a `u32`, **read-only to owners, non-persisted and non-hashed**: it is in no state block, no canonical byte string, no `state_hash` and no snapshot header (ADR-0005 § 2.4). `request_restore` and `request_new_game` set it **before** the first `restore()` or `init_world`; Save/Load supplies the value and persists it in `slot_epoch.bin` (ADR-0006), but the kernel's copy is the only one the simulation can see. It is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0005 § 2.3); a lint forbids any other read in `src/sim/`.

## Decision

### 1. Owners register `Callable`s; owners override nothing

An owner is any object (normally a `RefCounted`) that, during `BOOTING`, passes the kernel descriptors containing `Callable`s bound to its methods. There is no `BlockOwner` base class and nothing is overridden. Each owner method the kernel calls is declared `-> CompletionToken` and its last statement is `return ctx.complete()`.

The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies only to overrides, so it does not touch owner methods. The context classes of § 3 add methods to their base and **override none**; a Guideline forbids overriding a context method, because an override of `complete() -> CompletionToken` would fall under the rule. This also avoids `@abstract` (documented since 4.5, not needed) and lets tests register a plain stub. **Every override of a typed-return owner callable returns on all paths** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07)*: a stub or subclass that overrides an owner callable inherits `-> CompletionToken` (4.7 rule) and must end every branch in `return ctx.complete()`; an early `return` without it is an `INCOMPLETE`, and a path that falls off the end is a parse error or an `INCOMPLETE` by Verification 1. That GDScript rejects at parse time a typed function with a path that has no `return` is UNVERIFIED (Verification 1); whatever it shows, the token check (§ 3) is what catches a function that aborts at run time. At registration the kernel checks every `Callable` with `is_valid()` and, where available, `get_argument_count()` against the expected arity, so a wrong signature fails boot naming the registration rather than appearing later as `INCOMPLETE`.

### 2. A block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner; the kernel holds descriptors

The kernel never stores or inspects block data. It stores descriptors and calls the owner's callables. The owner's block object is a `RefCounted` with typed fields (packed arrays for struct-of-arrays state), never a `Resource` or `Node`. **`restore` copies into the existing block object and never replaces it**, because read views are long-lived facades over that object (§ 7); a test restores a block and checks its facade sees the restored values.

**Snapshot payload contract** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3, ADR-0006)*: every packed array an owner puts in a `snapshot` payload is a **duplicate** (`PackedXArray.duplicate()` or a freshly built array), never a live reference to the block's own array. The kernel reads the payload after `snapshot` returns, hashes it outside SAVING (ADR-0005) and may hold it while the owner keeps writing; a live reference would let a later mutator change a payload already encoded or queued for the writer. `restore` likewise copies out of `data` and keeps no reference into it. A test mutates the block after `snapshot` and checks the payload unchanged.

Every field is mandatory unless marked optional; a missing field fails boot naming the descriptor (CR-6: no silent defaults). GDScript reserves `class` as a keyword, so the GDD's `class` field is `block_class` in code.

**`BlockDescriptor`**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | `StringName` | Unique, namespaced (e.g. `&"graph.state"`) |
| `owner_name` | `StringName` | Registering system, for diagnostics |
| `schema_version` | `int` | Bumped on any serialised-shape change |
| `supported_versions` | `PackedInt32Array` | Versions `restore` accepts |
| `block_class` | `int` enum `SIM` / `PERCEPTION_OUT` | CR-12 |
| `persist` | `bool` | false = derived, rebuilt after load |
| `persist_scope` | `int` enum `WORLD` / `PROFILE` | Required when `persist` |
| `scope` | `int` enum `SHARED` / `PER_PLAYER` | PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId |
| `gameplay` | `bool` | The paused-write test (CR-16) |
| `interpolated` | `bool` | Kernel runs `commit_baseline` at P4 |
| `repl_hint` | `int` enum `HOST_ONLY` / `SHARED_SUMMARY` / `OWNER_PRIVATE` | Unused until VS-B, mandatory now |
| `restore_after` | `Array[StringName]` | DAG for ADR-0016 |
| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | `Callable` | Mandatory |
| `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` | `Callable` | Mandatory iff `interpolated` |
| `init_world`, `binding_source` | `Callable` | Optional (the binding source is this field only, never a separate registration) |

**`CommandTypeDescriptor`** (complete; ADR-0002 owns the meaning of each field)

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `type` | `StringName` |
| `owner_name` | `StringName` |
| `allowed_origins` | `int` bitmask (`ORIGIN_PLAYER = 1`, `ORIGIN_SYSTEM = 2`) |
| `actor_binding` | `int` enum `NONE` / `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` |
| `actor_source` | `StringName` (block id; empty iff `NONE`) |
| `coalesce` | `int` enum `NONE` / `LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` |
| `max_age_ticks` | `int` |
| `allowed_when_paused` | `bool` |
| `writes_blocks` | `Array[StringName]` |
| `payload_schema` | `Dictionary` (authoring form; compiled at registration, ADR-0002 § 3) |
| `validate`, `apply` | `Callable` |

**`HookDescriptor`**: `hook_id: StringName`, `owner_name: StringName`, `divisor: int` (≥ 1), `offset: int` (0 ≤ offset < divisor), `after: Array[Dictionary]` each `{&"id": StringName, &"tolerates_stale": bool}`, `callable: Callable`.

**`DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor`** (CR-6 via the Debug Overlay's E-DO-38): the field list is ADR-0031's; registration is here.

### 3. Contexts: reused, re-armed per call, non-re-entrant

Every kernel-invoked callable receives a context as its last argument and reports only through it. The kernel allocates **one context object per kind at boot and re-arms it before every call**; nothing is allocated per call. *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3.)* **One further kernel-internal `SnapshotContext`** serves hash reads (`block_hash`, `state_hash`) made **outside `SAVING`**, so a hash read never re-arms the context a save capture or a restore is using. It carries its own re-entrancy flag: a `block_hash` call made from inside a `snapshot` call (which would arm the same context twice) is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation and returns a not-ok result, never a hash. It is a kernel member under H1 `kernel_state` and is never exposed to owners.

```gdscript
class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
var completed: bool
var epoch: int
var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
	get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it

class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))

class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
var tick: int
func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
                                                    # file: src/kernel/facets/notify_context.gd (ADR-0010 § 1.1, TD-01): a presenter handler must name it
```

`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.

**Placement of `NotifyContext`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-01)*: the subscriber, result and control-outcome handler context lives in `src/kernel/facets/` with `CompletionToken`, `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyEvent` and the other types a presenter must name (ADR-0010 § 1.1, ADR-0004 placement table), because a presenter's handler signature `(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` has to compile in `src/presentation/`. The tick-phase contexts (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`) stay in kernel core and are on ADR-0010's presentation deny list; there is no `*Context` glob.

**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.

**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. The kernel holds the call result as a `Variant` and tests identity with `is_same()`, so a coroutine state returned by an owner that hit `await` fails the check like any other non-token value. Anything else, including `null`, a type default, a coroutine state or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).

### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty

```gdscript
class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
var phase: Phase
var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key layout: ADR-0004 § 3
func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void   # P5 event record; ADR-0004 § 5
func has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool           # true from the first granted open_for of that block until the scope is re-armed (ADR-0005 § 5.3)
func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
```

The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.

| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
|---|---|---|
| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |

`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.

`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. The debug-build check that catches a missed mark is ADR-0004 § 7 (it compares a block's hash with the kernel's `touch_serial` and with whether any key was marked, for blocks that do not declare `quiet_writes_allowed`); this ADR no longer states the rule. `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty`: it needs an open block and its records are discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE` and `CLOSED` (ADR-0004 § 5). `has_opened` is a pure read used by the kernel's hash path (ADR-0005 § 5.3): it never opens anything and never counts a violation. `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.

### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback

**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).

- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.

**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.

**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.

**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.

### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants

A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.

**Domain table** (static; new systems take the next free id; ids 32 and up are reserved for VS and later)

| Id | Domain | Id | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | kernel | 8 | interaction |
| 1 | save_load | 9 | suit |
| 2 | content data (item DB, templates, tuning) | 10 | assembly |
| 3 | graph | 11 | web_transit |
| 4 | layout | 12 | attention |
| 5 | body | 13 | horror |
| 6 | emitter | 14 | sanity |
| 7 | controller | 15–31 | presentation and tooling (read-view faults are diagnostics only) |

**Kernel fault codes (domain 0, closed)**

| Local | Name | Raised when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `INCOMPLETE` | a kernel-invoked callable did not return the armed token |
| 2 | `NO_OUTCOME` | `validate` called neither `ok()` nor `reject()` |
| 3 | `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` | the `LOADING` binding rebuild found a conflict or a binding-source fault |
| 4 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | a restore payload names an unregistered block |
| 5 | `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` | a payload was saved at another `TICK_RATE` |
| 6 | `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` | the supplied `restore_epoch` is out of range |
| 7 | `CAPTURE_ERROR` | a `SAVING` capture failed |
| 8 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | boot: duplicate block, command, hook, domain or channel id |
| 9 | `HOOK_CYCLE` | boot: a cycle in hook `after` edges |
| 10 | `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` | boot: unknown `after` hook, `restore_after` block or `writes_blocks` block, or a subscription to an unknown block (ADR-0004 § 2) |
| 11 | `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID` | boot: a command type's `actor_source` rule fails (CR-6) |
| 12 | `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN` | boot: a coalescing type allows both origins |
| 13 | `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_MISSING` | boot: a mandatory descriptor field is absent |
| 14 | `SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TOO_LONG` | boot: `lcm` of divisors exceeds `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` |
| 15 | `HOOK_OFFSET_INVALID` | boot: `divisor < 1` or `offset` not in `0..divisor-1` |
| 16 | `CALLABLE_SIGNATURE` | boot: a `Callable` is invalid or has the wrong arity |
| 17 | `MEMORY_BUDGET` | boot: the CR-17 joint memory assertion fails |

A P3 above `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is a **diagnostic** (it logs the slowest hooks), not a fault.

**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning), and, added 2026-10-28 and classified as ADR-0004 §§ 2, 3, 5 and 7 define them, `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` (a subscribe-time refusal, including the `PERCEPTION_OUT` rule of check 6), `DIRTY_KEY_INVALID`, `DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED`, `EVENT_OVERFLOW` and `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` (dev, playtest and test builds only). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.

Each owner's local code list is written with its system ADR (ADR-0011 onward); its domain id is fixed now.

### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet

The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).

`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get_view(block_id: StringName) -> Object` (never `get`: a method named `get` overrides the native `Object.get()`, which is a load-time parse error on 4.7.2, probed, and ADR-0010's `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE` rule), returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get_view` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get_view(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.

A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.

### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule

At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:

1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.

**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.

### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table

States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).

- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.

The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.

### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)

Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).

*(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07.)* The H1 **registries** group also holds, by name: `touch_serial` (a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`, written by every granted `open_for`; ADR-0004 § 7), the **hash-cache arrays** (`{hash, enc_len, serial}` as three parallel `PackedInt64Array`s sized once at the freeze; ADR-0005 §§ 5.1, 5.2), the per-block key-space table (ADR-0004 § 3) and the subscription tables (ADR-0004 § 2). **kernel_state** also holds the kernel-internal hash `SnapshotContext` of § 3 and the `kernel.clock` below. The H1 lint's fixed list is extended by exactly these names.

**The `kernel.clock` view.** `kernel.clock` is an H1 member owned by this ADR. It carries `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` and is exposed to modules and the composition root only as a read-only view (getters `tick()`, `world_seed()`, `restore_epoch()`; no setters). `T` advances only in the tick driver's boundary. **`world_seed`** is set before `INIT` (by `request_new_game`, or from the payload by `request_restore`) and does not change until the next new game or restore. **`restore_epoch`** is a `u32`, **read-only to owners, non-persisted and non-hashed**: it is in no state block, no canonical byte string, no `state_hash` and no snapshot header (ADR-0005 § 2.4). `request_restore` and `request_new_game` set it **before** the first `restore()` or `init_world`; Save/Load supplies the value and persists it in `slot_epoch.bin` (ADR-0006), but the kernel's copy is the only one the simulation can see. It is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0005 § 2.3); a lint forbids any other read in `src/sim/`.

  owner.setup(facet) ──► registrar.register_block(BlockDescriptor{... callables})

67	### 1. Owners register `Callable`s; owners override nothing
68	
69	An owner is any object (normally a `RefCounted`) that, during `BOOTING`, passes the kernel descriptors containing `Callable`s bound to its methods. There is no `BlockOwner` base class and nothing is overridden. Each owner method the kernel calls is declared `-> CompletionToken` and its last statement is `return ctx.complete()`.
70	
71	The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies only to overrides, so it does not touch owner methods. The context classes of § 3 add methods to their base and **override none**; a Guideline forbids overriding a context method, because an override of `complete() -> CompletionToken` would fall under the rule. This also avoids `@abstract` (documented since 4.5, not needed) and lets tests register a plain stub. **Every override of a typed-return owner callable returns on all paths** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07)*: a stub or subclass that overrides an owner callable inherits `-> CompletionToken` (4.7 rule) and must end every branch in `return ctx.complete()`; an early `return` without it is an `INCOMPLETE`, and a path that falls off the end is a parse error or an `INCOMPLETE` by Verification 1. That GDScript rejects at parse time a typed function with a path that has no `return` is UNVERIFIED (Verification 1); whatever it shows, the token check (§ 3) is what catches a function that aborts at run time. At registration the kernel checks every `Callable` with `is_valid()` and, where available, `get_argument_count()` against the expected arity, so a wrong signature fails boot naming the registration rather than appearing later as `INCOMPLETE`.
72	
73	### 2. A block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner; the kernel holds descriptors
74	
75	The kernel never stores or inspects block data. It stores descriptors and calls the owner's callables. The owner's block object is a `RefCounted` with typed fields (packed arrays for struct-of-arrays state), never a `Resource` or `Node`. **`restore` copies into the existing block object and never replaces it**, because read views are long-lived facades over that object (§ 7); a test restores a block and checks its facade sees the restored values.
76	
77	**Snapshot payload contract** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3, ADR-0006)*: every packed array an owner puts in a `snapshot` payload is a **duplicate** (`PackedXArray.duplicate()` or a freshly built array), never a live reference to the block's own array. The kernel reads the payload after `snapshot` returns, hashes it outside SAVING (ADR-0005) and may hold it while the owner keeps writing; a live reference would let a later mutator change a payload already encoded or queued for the writer. `restore` likewise copies out of `data` and keeps no reference into it. A test mutates the block after `snapshot` and checks the payload unchanged.
78	
79	Every field is mandatory unless marked optional; a missing field fails boot naming the descriptor (CR-6: no silent defaults). GDScript reserves `class` as a keyword, so the GDD's `class` field is `block_class` in code.

121	### 3. Contexts: reused, re-armed per call, non-re-entrant
122	
123	Every kernel-invoked callable receives a context as its last argument and reports only through it. The kernel allocates **one context object per kind at boot and re-arms it before every call**; nothing is allocated per call. *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3.)* **One further kernel-internal `SnapshotContext`** serves hash reads (`block_hash`, `state_hash`) made **outside `SAVING`**, so a hash read never re-arms the context a save capture or a restore is using. It carries its own re-entrancy flag: a `block_hash` call made from inside a `snapshot` call (which would arm the same context twice) is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation and returns a not-ok result, never a hash. It is a kernel member under H1 `kernel_state` and is never exposed to owners.
124	
125	```gdscript
126	class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
127	var completed: bool
128	var epoch: int
129	var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
130		get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
131	func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
132	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
133	func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it
134	
135	class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
136	func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
137	func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))
138	
139	class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
140	var tick: int
141	func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
142	func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
143	class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
144	class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
145	class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
146	                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
147	class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
148	                                                    # file: src/kernel/facets/notify_context.gd (ADR-0010 § 1.1, TD-01): a presenter handler must name it
149	```
150	
151	`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.
152	
153	**Placement of `NotifyContext`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-01)*: the subscriber, result and control-outcome handler context lives in `src/kernel/facets/` with `CompletionToken`, `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyEvent` and the other types a presenter must name (ADR-0010 § 1.1, ADR-0004 placement table), because a presenter's handler signature `(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` has to compile in `src/presentation/`. The tick-phase contexts (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`) stay in kernel core and are on ADR-0010's presentation deny list; there is no `*Context` glob.
154	
155	**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.
156	
157	**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. The kernel holds the call result as a `Variant` and tests identity with `is_same()`, so a coroutine state returned by an owner that hit `await` fails the check like any other non-token value. Anything else, including `null`, a type default, a coroutine state or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).

159	### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty
160	
161	```gdscript
162	class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
163	enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
164	var phase: Phase
165	var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
166	func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
167	func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key layout: ADR-0004 § 3
168	func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void   # P5 event record; ADR-0004 § 5
169	func has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool           # true from the first granted open_for of that block until the scope is re-armed (ADR-0005 § 5.3)
170	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
171	```
172	
173	The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.
174	
175	| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
176	|---|---|---|
177	| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
178	| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
179	| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
180	| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
181	| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
182	| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |

184	`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.

186	`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. The debug-build check that catches a missed mark is ADR-0004 § 7 (it compares a block's hash with the kernel's `touch_serial` and with whether any key was marked, for blocks that do not declare `quiet_writes_allowed`); this ADR no longer states the rule. `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty`: it needs an open block and its records are discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE` and `CLOSED` (ADR-0004 § 5). `has_opened` is a pure read used by the kernel's hash path (ADR-0005 § 5.3): it never opens anything and never counts a violation. `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.

188	### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback
189	
190	**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).
191	
192	- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
193	- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.
194	
195	**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.
196	
197	**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.
198	
199	**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.

246	### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet
247	
248	The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).
249	
250	`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get_view(block_id: StringName) -> Object` (never `get`: a method named `get` overrides the native `Object.get()`, which is a load-time parse error on 4.7.2, probed, and ADR-0010's `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE` rule), returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get_view` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get_view(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.
251	
252	A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.
253	
254	### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule
255	
256	At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:
257	
258	1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
259	2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
260	3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
261	4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.
262	
263	**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.

265	### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table
266	
267	States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).
268	
269	- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
270	- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
271	- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
272	- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
273	- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.
274	
275	The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.

277	### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)
278	
279	Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).
280	
281	*(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07.)* The H1 **registries** group also holds, by name: `touch_serial` (a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`, written by every granted `open_for`; ADR-0004 § 7), the **hash-cache arrays** (`{hash, enc_len, serial}` as three parallel `PackedInt64Array`s sized once at the freeze; ADR-0005 §§ 5.1, 5.2), the per-block key-space table (ADR-0004 § 3) and the subscription tables (ADR-0004 § 2). **kernel_state** also holds the kernel-internal hash `SnapshotContext` of § 3 and the `kernel.clock` below. The H1 lint's fixed list is extended by exactly these names.
282	
283	**The `kernel.clock` view.** `kernel.clock` is an H1 member owned by this ADR. It carries `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` and is exposed to modules and the composition root only as a read-only view (getters `tick()`, `world_seed()`, `restore_epoch()`; no setters). `T` advances only in the tick driver's boundary. **`world_seed`** is set before `INIT` (by `request_new_game`, or from the payload by `request_restore`) and does not change until the next new game or restore. **`restore_epoch`** is a `u32`, **read-only to owners, non-persisted and non-hashed**: it is in no state block, no canonical byte string, no `state_hash` and no snapshot header (ADR-0005 § 2.4). `request_restore` and `request_new_game` set it **before** the first `restore()` or `init_world`; Save/Load supplies the value and persists it in `slot_epoch.bin` (ADR-0006), but the kernel's copy is the only one the simulation can see. It is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0005 § 2.3); a lint forbids any other read in `src/sim/`.
284	
285	### Architecture Diagram
286	
287	```
288	BOOTING (ModuleFacet.registrar, one-way; nulled at the freeze)
289	  owner.setup(facet) ──► registrar.register_block(BlockDescriptor{... callables})
